# 2 Baruch Chapter 31 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** Second Fast and Dialogue

---

**1** I went back to the people and gathered them together — young and old alike — and spoke to them:

**2** "Listen, O Israel! Pay attention, O Jacob! Hear me, all you who work the land:

**3** The grief over our mother city Zion and the suffering that has come to Jerusalem — all of it has now fallen on us. Both have been taken away from us. But don't waste your tears on Zion's enemies — their fate is even more bitter than ours. Don't mourn for those who attacked her — they will vanish soon enough.

**4** Instead, weep over your own sins. That is why this suffering has come upon you.

**5** But if you will set your ways right, and walk the road of righteousness, you will leave this age quickly — it won't last long for you."

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic rendering. Baruch's pastoral address is direct and urgent. The rhetorical move is striking: don't grieve for Babylon/Rome, grieve for your own sin. The promise in v.5 is indirect but real — righteous living leads to a quick departure from this suffering age.*
